blocking_issues: experiments/transfer_cube/freeze/autogreedy.json, freeze/REQUEST.json and DEVIATIONS.md do not disclose that the auto-greedy edit IS one of the agent's own candidates. The frozen auto-greedy ops (enc0.h1 x0 + enc3.h4 x2) are op-for-op identical to candidate r2 in stage3/candidates.json, which the agent wrote by hand in the refinement round. Before the search script was rewritten (a58d08c, 12:44), the agent had already measured r2 on all 1,000 design seeds (121 fixed / 22 broken, +9.9, which includes the search seeds 20500 to 20949) and on the 500 validation seeds (61 / 23, +7.6; validation finished about 12:41). I recomputed both. The committed-but-never-run version (da0c746) was forced to start from cross.h1.x0, so it could not have returned this pair. The rewrite from one forced start to all 15 pairs was made after r2's results were known. The docstring section 'What the author had seen' and the DEVIATIONS entry name only c08 and, generically, 'the validation results', and REQUEST.json says only that the auto-greedy edit 'shares one head with the agent's edit'. SPEC.md Stage 4 describes this arm as one the agent 'never saw', and the Controls table uses it as the 'you do not need an LLM' control. That description does not hold here and the package does not correct it. The rewrite appears to have made the rival stronger, so I am not claiming it was rigged; the issue is that the control's independence is overstated. To settle it, before the tag: append to DEVIATIONS.md, and state in REQUEST.json (and in edit.json or PROGRESS.md if convenient), that autogreedy equals candidate r2, give r2's design and validation numbers, say these were known before the rewrite, and say that the report must not describe the arm as an independent no-LLM result.
